items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: you had Chick Webb, Teddy Hill, and they had a little group up there called the Savoy Sultans

ctx.x: Was there ever a time where you went face to face, a battle with the Ellington band?

I can’t say that we did. We did with the Lionel Hampton band. He always wanted to choose Basie because he said his band was better than Basie’s band, we could swing better and everything. So, we just had it out at the Savoy one night. And he never did do that anymore. But you were well entertained when you would go to the Savoy and you had Chick Webb, Teddy Hill, and they had a little group up there called the Savoy Sultans and they’d wear you out. There was only about eight of them but they sounded like 80.…
And you were playing virtually exclusively for dancing, correct?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: Dizzy went with Teddy Hill. ... He was with Teddy Hill.

ctx.x: Well, had you given him any trouble or --

No. Well, Charlie and Rama had played with Dizzy so they wanted somebody in the band that they had played with. You know, they were good buddies. And I'm from St. Louis, you know. But Dizzy and I got in a little -- we started playing some "Body and Soul" in a place in Philadelphia one night and I kind of made a little noise that night, playing "Body and Soul." So Lucky hired me back. And Dizzy went with Teddy Hill. Come the side 3 - end

But after we went from Philadelphia back to New York, that's when Bobby Moore took ill and I -- Herschel and Jo, they recommended me to Basie and I took his place, you know. And -- oh, that was the latter part of 1937. But I still wanted to learn more about music because when I joined Basie's band, it was nothing but head arrangements. Everything was head arrangements. They didn't have -- I bet they didn't have 10 manuscripts, you know.
